current_evidence: The council's 'What to submit with your planning application' page links this PDF as its only 'Local validation list' (pdf, 469.07 KB) and says it 'has been updated to include new requirements for biodiversity net gain'. Searches found no newer version; the only other version found, on the democracy site, is a 2010 consultation copy.

issues.detail: The list date of 2025-02-01 comes only from the upload folder in the URL ('Date basis: url path (upload month)'), not from any adoption or publication date in the text. The planning page gives no date, so the actual adoption or effective date is unverified.
issues.evidence: Planning page: 'Our local validation list has been updated to include new requirements for biodiversity net gain' (no date given).

issues.detail: 12 of the 13 tab_items are taken from the superseded November 2023 list (Validation-list-nov-2023.pdf) rather than the current 2025-02 list. The two documents were mixed in one tab.

The drawing-standards item 'The location plan should ideally be provided on a separate sheet of paper...' appears twice, once from the 2023 list and once from the 2025 list. Both copies are cut off mid-word ('suggestive scale 1:200 o').

Several tab items are URL fragments, headings or policy lists rather than requirements. Examples: 'Dwellings 0330/BR_PDF_AD_M1_2015_with_2016_amendments_V3.pdf [Go to checklist:'; 'National Marine Policy Statement: 322/pb3654-marine-policy-statement-110316.pdf Draft South West Marine Plan:'; 'National Design Guide paragraphs 69 and 70: 3468/National_Design_Guide.pdf ...'; 'Special Protected Areas (SPA)*'; and 'Policy background Joint Local Plan Policy DEV2 ... DEV28 (Trees, woodlands and hedge'.
issues.evidence: Grokbot tab_items under 'Submission rules' and 'Policy-driven requirements'.

issues.detail: Several app-type rows carry trigger text taken from a different item. Open space / play space uses the tail of the Community Involvement Statement trigger ('proposed on playing fields; or, Onshore wind developments...'). Environmental Statement (EIA) uses the same SCI trigger list. Sequential / Exception Test (flood) uses the retail town-centre sequential test text. Schedule of works (listed building) uses a roof-plan drawing note ('drawing and schedule of works'). Pre-application advice uses BNG text. Waste / refuse storage uses a noise-assessment clause about night-time deliveries within 100m. Highways / visibility splays uses the site-plan drawing description.
issues.evidence: Grokbot app_type_rows trigger_excerpt fields, e.g. Sequential/Exception Test (flood): 'should include a sequential test ... sequentially preferable sites in and on the edge of existing and proposed centres'.

issues.detail: Many triggers are cut off or garbled and give no usable threshold. Drainage Strategy reads 'When this item is required: OFFICIAL:SENSITIVE 1.' Flood Risk Assessment reads 'Where or when this item is required: Flood Risk Assessment 1.' Air Quality Assessment is mixed with nationally described space standards text and cut off at 'Wher'. HRA reads 'When or where this is required;' with nothing after it. Ecological Survey reads 'by an Ecological Impact Assessment (EcIA).' Planning Statement reads 'plan and a planning statement.' Crime prevention quotes a Secured by Design principle instead of a trigger. Housing mix / accessible dwellings gives no threshold.

The Design and Access Statement and Heritage Statement rows are placed under Advertisement consent. Grokbot's own excerpt shows both items listed before the '3.4 ADVERTISEMENT CONSENT' heading. They therefore belong to the preceding application-type checklist (3.3), not to advertisement consent, whose checklist lists only application form, location plan, plans and drawings, and fee.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: 'Design and Access Statement [guidance] You will need to check the Local Validation List ... 3.4 ADVERTISEMENT CONSENT Validation Checklist Criteria Application form [guidance] Location plan [guidance] Plans and Drawings [guidance] correct fee'.

issues.detail: The Viability Assessment row is placed under Outline with the note 'Application type named in requirement text', but the quoted text does not mention outline applications.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: 'a detailed Viability Assessment is required to be submitted with the planning application as outlined in para 57 of the NPPF'.

issues.detail: About 38 rows are tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. Examples: Tree Survey, Archaeological Assessment, Contaminated Land, Noise, Fire Statement, Tall Buildings Report and Town Centre justification. The list contains its own per-application-type checklists (sections 3.x), so applicability should come from those rather than being guessed. Several items apply by site circumstance (trees, contamination, archaeology) across householder, outline and other types.
issues.evidence: Excerpt references '3.4 ADVERTISEMENT CONSENT Validation Checklist Criteria', showing that application-type checklists 3.1-3.3 exist.

issues.detail: Householder, Listed building consent, Reserved matters and other types are shown as '(none)'. The list has dedicated application-type validation checklists, and site-based items such as Tree Survey (trees on or next to the site), the HRA recreational-pressure bed-space information ('If your development is proposing new bed spaces') and Archaeological Assessment are not limited to full applications. This could not be verified item by item because the PDF is blocked.
issues.evidence: Grokbot tab item: 'Recreational pressure only If your development is proposing new bed spaces, we require the quantity so the LPA can complete a HRA'.

issues.detail: The BNG trigger quotes only 'mandatory requirement for a minimum 10% BNG will apply to planning applications for major development from 12th February 2024'. This omits that statutory BNG has also applied to small (minor) sites since 2 April 2024, and the row is filed under Full planning only.
issues.evidence: Grokbot BNG trigger_excerpt; national BNG commencement for small sites 2 April 2024.

summary: The workbook link is the PDF the council's planning page currently links. However, WebFetch is blocked from reading it (robots_disallowed), so its contents and date could not be checked against the source, and the issues above come from Grokbot's own extracted text. That text shows mismatched and cut-off triggers, tab items mixed from the superseded Nov 2023 list, and Design and Access and Heritage Statements wrongly filed under advertisement consent.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
